He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]]. ==High school career== Riley attended high school at Southwest Academy Prep in [[London, Ontario]] with brief stops at [[Preston High School (Ontario)|Preston High School]] and [[Grand River Collegiate Institute]].{{cite web |last=Bryson |first=Mark |title=Kitchener's Will Riley hot in pursuit of NBA dream |url=https://www.therecord.com/sports/basketball/kitcheners-will-riley-hot-in-pursuit-of-nba-dream/article_3de361ba-23aa-53d9-882f-609ab80f648c.html |website=The Record |access-date=September 23, 2024 |date=March 2, 2024}} He then attended [[The Phelps School]] in [[Malvern, Pennsylvania]] where he spent the last two years of his high school career. He averaged 21.9 points, 4.7 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game in the [[EYBL]] and was named Offensive MVP of the EYBL Indy Session, starring for UPlay Canada.{{cite web |title=Riley Signs with Illinois |url=https://fightingillini.com/news/2024/6/23/mens-basketball-riley-signs-with-illinois.aspx |website=University of Illinois Athletics |access-date=September 23, 2024 |language=en |date=June 23, 2024}} He was named MVP of the 2024 [[Basketball Without Borders]] Global Camp during [[NBA All-Star weekend]].{{cite web |title=Canadian Will Riley named MVP of BWB Global camp |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/canadian-will-riley-named-mvp-of-bwb-global-camp |website=FIBA.basketball |date=February 19, 2024 |access-date=September 23, 2024 |language=en}} ===Recruiting=== He was ranked as the top-ranked Canadian prospect and No. 9 overall by [[247Sports]], No. 10 by [[On3.com|On3]] and No. 11 by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] in the class of 2025. On June 23, 2024, Riley committed to [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]]. He was originally part of the class of 2025 but reclassified to 2024 to join earlier. At the time of his signing, Riley was the highest-ranked recruit signed by [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] in the internet era, surpassing [[Dee Brown (basketball, born 1984)|Dee Brown]] from the class of 2002. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|collapse=no|year=2024}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Will Riley | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Kitchener, ON]] | highschool = [[The Phelps School]] | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 180 | 40 = | commitdate = 6/23/24 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn rank = | espn stars = 5 | On3 stars = 5 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2024 | rivals ref title = 2024 Illinois Commits | scout ref title = Men's Basketball Recruiting | espn ref title = ESPN- Illinois Fighting Illini Men's Basketball Recruiting | rivals school = Illinois | 247 school = Illinois | scout s = | espn schoolid = 356 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 11 | espn overall = | 247 overall = 10 | accessdate = | bball = yes |On3 overall = 20 |On3 school = Illinois-fighting-illini }} ==College career== On November 11, 2024, Riley was named the first [[2024–25 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season#Players of the week|Big Ten Freshman of the Week for the 2024–25 season]]. Riley's overall week (averaging 22.5 points and seven rebounds per game) in two Illinois wins, as well as his securing the Illini freshman scoring record, tipped the scales in his favor.{{Cite web |last=Langendorf |first=Jason |date=2024-11-11 |title=Illinois Guard Will Riley Named Big Ten Freshman of the Week |url=https://www.si.com/college/illinois/basketball/will-riley-big-ten-freshman-of-the-week-illinois |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en-US}} He went on to receive the award twice more.{{Cite web |date=2026-02-21 |title=Riley Nabs Third B1G Freshman of the Week Accolade Following the [[Big Ten]] regular season's conclusion, he was named Big Ten Sixth Man of the Year.{{Cite web |last=Werner |first=Jeremy |date=2025-03-12 |title=Illini freshman Will Riley wins Big Ten |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=ESPN.com}} ==Professional career== In the [[2025 NBA draft]], Riley was selected 21st overall by the [[Utah Jazz]] and traded to the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web |last=Mittal |first=Sahil |date=2025-06-25 |title=Will Riley drafted No. 21 by Utah Jazz, traded to Washington Wizards |url=https://dailyillini.com/sports-stories/mens-sports/men-basketball/2025/06/25/will-riley-drafted-no-21-by-utah-jazz-traded-to-washington-wizards/ |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=The Daily Illini}} He made his professional debut with the Wizards on October 22, 2025, scoring two points in a 133–120 loss against the [[2025–26 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Will Riley Stats|access-date=December 5, 2025|website=basketball-reference.com |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/rileywi01.html}} On April 5, 2026, Riley became the first Wizards rookie since [[Calbert Cheaney]] in February 1994 to record consecutive 30-point games.{{Cite web |last=Ghafir |first=Ahmed |date=2026-04-06 |title=Will Riley Shines for Short-Handed Wizards to Make History |url=https://roundtable.io/sports/nba/wizards/players/will-riley-shines-for-short-handed-wizards-to-make-history |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=RoundtableSports |language=en}} Additionally, Riley became the youngest player since Lebron James in 2004 to record at least 30 points and five steals in one game. ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics
